title: The Secret Rose Garden
author: Mahmud Shabistari (Lederer trans)
description: The Secret Rose Garden (Gulshan-i Raz) of Sa'd ud Din Mahmud Shabistari, rendered from the Persian with an introduction by Florence Lederer (London: John Murray, Wisdom of the East series, 1920). Mahmud Shabistari (c. 1288-1340), a Sufi of Tabriz, composed this didactic poem of about a thousand couplets around 1317 in answer to fifteen questions on Sufi doctrine sent by a scholar from Herat. The answers concern thought and reflection, the self and the 'I', the traveller and the Perfect Man, the nature of union, the meaning of the sea and its pearls, and the symbolic vocabulary of Sufi poetry: the eye and lip, the curl, the cheek and mole, wine, the tavern, the idol, the girdle and the Christian boy. Drawing on Ibn Arabi's unity of being, it is a compact handbook of Sufi metaphysics and symbolism. Lederer offers a free poetic version emphasising its devotional meaning.
